patterns.title: Asymmetric Structure
patterns.summary: A structural condition where comparable regions receive unequal rule, constraint, or authority application without a declared differentiation rule.

patterns.title: Authority Collision
patterns.summary: A structural condition where multiple authorities claim governance over the same region without a declared precedence or resolution rule.

patterns.title: Authority Merge Conflict
patterns.summary: A structural condition where multiple authority states are combined over a shared scope without a declared merge, precedence, or reconciliation rule.

patterns.title: Authority Shadowing
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a declared authority is functionally overridden by another authority without an explicit override rule.

patterns.title: Authority-State Mismatch
patterns.summary: A structural condition where observed system state no longer aligns with the declared authority state that is supposed to govern it.

patterns.title: Boundary Leakage
patterns.summary: A structural condition where effects, permissions, state, data, or authority cross a declared boundary without an authorized exception.

patterns.title: Circular Dependency
patterns.summary: A structural condition where two or more elements depend on each other in a closed loop without an independent base condition or declared resolution mechanism.

patterns.title: Compatibility Violation
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a graph, object, behavior, or runtime state exceeds a declared compatibility envelope without an authorized exception.

patterns.title: Constraints Underspecified
patterns.summary: A structural condition where declared constraints are insufficient to eliminate ambiguity or multiple admissible states.

patterns.title: Contract Drift
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a declared contract changes but connected structures, implementations, consumers, or expectations do not update in sync.

patterns.title: Convergence Failure
patterns.summary: A structural condition where sequential or parallel states fail to resolve into an equivalent or coherent structure under shared authority and constraints.

patterns.title: Cross-Layer Escalation
patterns.summary: A structural condition where escalation originating in one layer propagates into another authority, boundary, or control layer without explicit authorization.

patterns.title: Density Spike
patterns.summary: A structural condition where nodes, edges, dependencies, decisions, or effects concentrate sharply within a localized region beyond declared thresholds.

patterns.title: Density Vacuum
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a region expected to contain sufficient nodes, edges, coverage, or relationships falls below declared density thresholds.

patterns.title: Divergent Outputs
patterns.summary: A structural condition where parallel evaluations under comparable scope and shared authority produce non-equivalent outputs.

patterns.title: Escalation Growth
patterns.summary: A structural condition where impact, authority, scope, or consequence increases across sequential states without a declared limiting mechanism.

patterns.title: Incomplete Declaration
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an element is declared but required attributes, dependencies, or linked definitions are missing.

patterns.title: Interface Mismatch
patterns.summary: A structural condition where observed interface behavior, shape, or exchange differs from the declared interface contract.

patterns.title: Invariant Breakage
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an observed state violates a declared invariant that is supposed to remain true.

patterns.title: Missing Authority
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a region, action, state, or decision path exists without a declared governing authority.

patterns.title: Non-Deterministic Execution
patterns.summary: A structural condition where equivalent inputs and declared constraints produce divergent outputs across executions.

patterns.title: Orphaned Structure
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a node, region, object, state, or declaration exists without linkage to the governing graph or integration pathway.

patterns.title: Overreach
patterns.summary: A structural condition where actions, effects, authority, or modifications extend beyond declared scope without authorization.

patterns.title: Persistence Instability
patterns.summary: A structural condition where persisted state cannot be stored and restored into an equivalent structure without alteration.

patterns.title: Propagation Amplification
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an effect, declaration, authority, constraint, or state increases in scope or intensity as it propagates beyond declared bounds.

patterns.title: Redundant Declaration
patterns.summary: A structural condition where multiple declarations produce equivalent structural effect without semantic differentiation.

patterns.title: Reference Instability
patterns.summary: A structural condition where references, identifiers, links, or anchors change across equivalent evaluations without a declared cause.

patterns.title: Schema Breakage
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an instance, graph, payload, or object violates the type, shape, or rule requirements of a declared schema.

patterns.title: Silent Mutation
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a change occurs without a corresponding declared update, authority update, or version change.

patterns.title: Threshold Breach
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an observed metric, value, state, or condition exceeds a declared quantitative or qualitative threshold.

patterns.title: Unbounded Scope
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an operation, authority, rule, or expansion has no declared upper bound, boundary, or termination condition.

patterns.title: Unconstrained Expansion
patterns.summary: A structural condition where a region, process, authority, or effect expands without governing constraints limiting growth.

patterns.title: Undeclared Side Effect
patterns.summary: A structural condition where an operation modifies regions outside its declared target scope without a declared propagation or side-effect rule.

lenses.title: Absence Lens
lenses.summary: Detects structurally required elements that are missing from the observed structure.

lenses.title: Authority Overlay Lens
lenses.summary: Maps declared authority hierarchies onto observed structure to detect absence, override, or conflict.

lenses.title: Boundary Compliance Lens
lenses.summary: Evaluates observed structure against declared boundary posture, including allow, block, and exception rules.

lenses.title: Compatibility Envelope Lens
lenses.summary: Determines whether structure fits within declared runtime, platform, version, or support constraints.

lenses.title: Compression Lens
lenses.summary: Reduces structural graphs into stable minimal representations for comparison, redundancy detection, and diffing.

lenses.title: Conflict Lens
lenses.summary: Detects mutually incompatible constraints, claims, states, or declarations that cannot be simultaneously satisfied.

lenses.title: Constraint Sufficiency Lens
lenses.summary: Evaluates whether declared constraints are sufficient to eliminate structural degrees of freedom.

lenses.title: Convergence Lens
lenses.summary: Compares parallel structural systems to determine whether they align under shared authority.

lenses.title: Determinism Lens
lenses.summary: Evaluates whether identical structural inputs produce equivalent structural outputs across repeated executions.

lenses.title: Escalation Gradient Lens
lenses.summary: Measures structural growth or intensification across sequential executions, states, or transitions.

lenses.title: Interface Contract Lens
lenses.summary: Compares declared interface structure to observed runtime structure to detect contract deviations.

lenses.title: Invariant Lens
lenses.summary: Verifies that declared invariants are structurally enforceable and not contradicted by observed structure.

lenses.title: Isolation Boundary Lens
lenses.summary: Evaluates whether structural constraints, effects, and regions remain contained within declared boundaries.

lenses.title: Normalization Lens
lenses.summary: Transforms structurally equivalent variants into a canonical form to prevent false divergence.

lenses.title: Overreach Lens
lenses.summary: Detects structure that exceeds declared scope or authority reach.

lenses.title: Propagation Lens
lenses.summary: Traces how structural declarations, effects, or state changes propagate across boundaries or stages.

lenses.title: Provenance Trace Lens
lenses.summary: Attaches stable lineage to structural regions by mapping origin, reference history, and transformation path.

lenses.title: Reconciliation Lens
lenses.summary: Evaluates whether structural changes align with declared authority updates, version changes, or reconciliation rules.

lenses.title: Reference Stability Lens
lenses.summary: Evaluates whether structural references, identifiers, nodes, and edges remain consistent across execution cycles or comparable states.

lenses.title: Variance / Entropy Lens
lenses.summary: Measures structural variability across repeated or comparable evaluations and identifies divergence beyond expected bounds.

categories.title: Agents
categories.summary: Problems where agent behavior expands, acts outside intent, fails to finish, modifies state, or chooses actions without enough stable control.

categories.title: Changes & Versions
categories.summary: Problems where model behavior, prompts, contracts, schemas, outputs, references, rubrics, or expectations change without the surrounding workflow updating correctly.

categories.title: Coverage & Guidance
categories.summary: Problems where prompts, rubrics, diagnostics, fallback rules, examples, requirements, or relationship maps are incomplete, underspecified, or missing needed guidance.

categories.title: Duplication & Overload
categories.summary: Problems where fields, sections, rules, checks, prompts, workflow steps, or review queues become duplicated, overloaded, bottlenecked, or carry too many meanings.

categories.title: Inconsistent Behavior
categories.summary: Problems where similar inputs, repeated attempts, validations, prompts, routes, or cases produce different results without a clear reason.

categories.title: Loops & Resolution
categories.summary: Problems where agents, workflows, reviews, approvals, policies, schemas, or routing paths loop, wait on themselves, fail to settle, or cannot identify a final state.

categories.title: MCP, Tools & Integrations
categories.summary: Problems involving tool calls, MCP surfaces, integration contracts, required tool inputs, tool results, parser consumers, or downstream systems that depend on AI output.

categories.title: Memory & Context
categories.summary: Problems where task state, prior instructions, saved memory, restored context, stale information, or cross-task context affects behavior incorrectly.

categories.title: Output
categories.summary: Problems where generated content, citations, fields, formats, parser-facing output, or structured responses are missing, malformed, unsupported, or unusable.

categories.title: Permissions & Approvals
categories.summary: Problems where ownership, approval, authority, permission state, responsible control, or action rights are missing, stale, bypassed, conflicting, or unclear.

categories.title: Rules & Policies
categories.summary: Problems where prompts, policies, rules, roles, constraints, or declared behavior conflict, drift, duplicate each other, or fail to match actual behavior.

categories.title: Scope & Boundaries
categories.summary: Problems where tasks, files, context, retrieval, permissions, actions, or outputs cross limits, use outside information, or lack clear operating boundaries.

categories.title: Spread & Escalation
categories.summary: Problems where small errors, local exceptions, risk signals, retries, permissions, or outputs spread downstream, grow in consequence, or trigger broader actions.

categories.title: Workflow & Handoffs
categories.summary: Problems where review steps, handoffs, task progress, workflow ownership, downstream steps, or process coordination break, loop, disagree, or lose resolution.
